title: Cylindrical surfaces and generators
terms: cylinder; right circular cylinder; elliptic cylinder; parabolic cylinder; generator; element of a cylinder.

exposition.text:
A cylindrical surface is the union of lines through a base curve, all parallel to a fixed nonzero
direction called its generator direction; these individual lines are its elements. The cylinder
2 2
need not be circular. An equation independent of z, such as x + 4y = 1, describes a surface
invariant under translation along the z-axis.
For an oblique cylinder, parameterize a base point P(s) and write P (s) + tv. Eliminate s, t using
linear combinations constant along v. This is more reliable than assuming a missing coordinate:
only axis-parallel cylinders necessarily have a missing coordinate in the given Cartesian system.
A right circular cylinder has circular sections perpendicular to its axis. An elliptic cylinder has
2 2 2 2
elliptical perpendicular sections; an axis-aligned example is x /a + y /b = 1 with z free. A
2
parabolic cylinder, such as z = x with y free, is obtained by translating a parabola. A tilted
section of a circular cylinder can be an ellipse even though its perpendicular sections are circles.

question.text:
2 2
The surface (x − z) + 4(y + 2z) = 1 is a cylinder. Which vector gives a generator direction?
(A) (1, 2, 1) (B) (1, −2, 1) (C) (1, −2, −1) (D) (2, 1, 1) (E) (0, 0, 1)

solution.text:
A generator preserves x − z and y + 2z. Its direction (a, b, c) therefore satisfies a − c = 0 and
b + 2c = 0, hence is proportional to (1, −2, 1).

question.text:
Which surface is a circular cylinder with axis parallel to (1, 0, 0)?

2 2 2 2 2

2 2 2

solution.text:
The selected equation is independent of x and has circular yz cross-sections centered at
(1, −2) with radius 3. Thus varying x traces its generators.
